title: Static synchronized vs instance synchronized — different locks, can run simultaneously
shortTitle: What is static vs instance synchronized?

s1_definition.profdef: A `static synchronized` method locks on the **Class object** (`ClassName.class`). An `instance synchronized` method locks on the **instance** (`this`). These are TWO DIFFERENT locks — so they can execute SIMULTANEOUSLY. A thread calling a static synchronized method does NOT block a thread calling an instance synchronized method on the same object, and vice versa. This surprises many developers who assume "synchronized = only one thread in any synchronized method." That's only true for methods using the SAME lock object.
s1_definition.analogy: The bank has TWO padlocks: one on the MAIN VAULT DOOR (Class lock — shared by all branches) and one on RAJESH'S DRAWER (instance lock — specific to Rajesh's account). A teller locking the vault door does NOT prevent another teller from opening Rajesh's drawer — they're different padlocks. Both operations happen simultaneously. Only when two tellers try to lock the SAME padlock does one wait.
s1_definition.oneliner: static synchronized = locks Class object. instance synchronized = locks `this`. DIFFERENT locks → run in PARALLEL. Same lock type → mutual exclusion.
s1_definition.raw:
**Professional definition:** A `static synchronized` method locks on the **Class object** (`ClassName.class`). An `instance synchronized` method locks on the **instance** (`this`). These are TWO DIFFERENT locks — so they can execute SIMULTANEOUSLY. A thread calling a static synchronized method does NOT block a thread calling an instance synchronized method on the same object, and vice versa. This surprises many developers who assume "synchronized = only one thread in any synchronized method." That's only true for methods using the SAME lock object.

**In simple words (banking analogy):** The bank has TWO padlocks: one on the MAIN VAULT DOOR (Class lock — shared by all branches) and one on RAJESH'S DRAWER (instance lock — specific to Rajesh's account). A teller locking the vault door does NOT prevent another teller from opening Rajesh's drawer — they're different padlocks. Both operations happen simultaneously. Only when two tellers try to lock the SAME padlock does one wait.

**One line to remember:** static synchronized = locks Class object. instance synchronized = locks `this`. DIFFERENT locks → run in PARALLEL. Same lock type → mutual exclusion.

sections.s3_banking: **Problem — The AccountService had a `static synchronized generateDailyReport()` and an `instance synchronized debit()`.** A developer assumed the daily report would block all debit operations (safe for consistency). But static sync and instance sync use DIFFERENT locks — debits continued during report generation, producing an inconsistent report. Fix: use the SAME lock for both: `private static final Object GLOBAL_LOCK = new Object()` — both methods synchronize on GLOBAL_LOCK.

sections.s5_journey:
**Step 1.** Thread-1 calls `AccountService.globalAudit()` → acquires lock on `AccountService.class` → holds for 500ms.

**Step 2.** Thread-2 calls `service.debit(1000)` → tries to acquire lock on `this` (the instance) → DIFFERENT lock from Class → acquires immediately → debit executes in <1ms. NOT blocked by the static method!

**Step 3.** Thread-3 calls `service.getBalance()` → tries to acquire lock on `this` → SAME lock as debit() → if debit is running, Thread-3 is BLOCKED.

**Step 4.** Thread-4 calls `priya.debit(2000)` on a DIFFERENT instance → lock on `priya` (different object) → NOT blocked by `rajesh.debit()`. Different instances = different locks = parallel.
sections.s5b_flow:
```
  ═══ LOCK MATRIX ═══

  Method A                    Method B                  Same Lock?  Parallel?
  ─────────────────────────  ──────────────────────── ─────────── ─────────
  static synchronized        instance synchronized     NO (Class vs this) YES!
  instance sync (obj1)       instance sync (obj1)      YES (same this)    NO!
  instance sync (obj1)       instance sync (obj2)      NO (diff this)     YES!
  static sync (ClassA)       static sync (ClassA)      YES (same Class)   NO!
  static sync (ClassA)       static sync (ClassB)      NO (diff Class)    YES!

  ═══ TWO DIFFERENT LOCKS ═══

  Thread-1: static synchronized → lock on [AccountService.class]
  Thread-2: instance synchronized → lock on [this]
  ← DIFFERENT locks → both execute simultaneously!
```
sections.s5c_hld:
```
  ═══ HLD — Lock Separation in Banking Service ═══

  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  AccountService                                   │
  │                                                    │
  │  CLASS LOCK (AccountService.class):               │
  │  ├─ static synchronized globalAudit()             │
  │  ├─ static synchronized loadConfig()              │
  │  └─ ONE thread at a time for ALL static methods   │
  │                                                    │
  │  INSTANCE LOCK (this):                            │
  │  ├─ synchronized debit()     ← per-instance lock  │
  │  ├─ synchronized getBalance()                      │
  │  └─ ONE thread per instance for instance methods  │
  │                                                    │
  │  globalAudit() and debit() → DIFFERENT locks      │
  │  → CAN run simultaneously! (potential bug!)       │
  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```
sections.s5d_lld:
```
  ═══ LLD — Static vs Instance Monitor Locks ═══

  ┌──────────────────────────────────────┐
  │    AccountService.class object       │  ← ONE per JVM
  │  Monitor: {                          │
  │    owner: Thread-1 (globalAudit)     │
  │    entrySet: [Thread-3]              │  static sync methods wait here
  │  }                                    │
  └──────────────────────────────────────┘

  ┌──────────────────────────────────────┐
  │    accountService instance (this)    │  ← ONE per instance
  │  Monitor: {                          │
  │    owner: Thread-2 (debit)           │
  │    entrySet: [Thread-4]              │  instance sync methods wait here
  │  }                                    │
  └──────────────────────────────────────┘

  Thread-1 holds CLASS lock → does NOT block Thread-2 (holds INSTANCE lock)
  Thread-2 holds INSTANCE lock → does NOT block Thread-1 (holds CLASS lock)

  FIX (if mutual exclusion needed across both):
  private static final Object SHARED_LOCK = new Object();
  static void globalAudit() { synchronized(SHARED_LOCK) { ... } }
  void debit(amt)            { synchronized(SHARED_LOCK) { ... } }
  // Now BOTH methods use the SAME lock → mutual exclusion!
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
A static synchronized method locks on the Class object (`ClassName.class`). An instance synchronized method locks on `this` (the specific instance). These are TWO DIFFERENT locks — so a static synchronized method and an instance synchronized method CAN execute simultaneously on the same object. This surprises many developers who expect synchronized to mean "only one thread in any synchronized method." That's only true for methods sharing the SAME lock.

The lock matrix: static sync + static sync (same class) → same Class lock → blocked. Instance sync + instance sync (same object) → same `this` lock → blocked. Instance sync on obj1 + instance sync on obj2 → different `this` → parallel. Static sync + instance sync → different locks (Class vs this) → parallel. In banking: if globalAudit() (static sync) needs to prevent debits (instance sync) during the report, both must use the SAME lock object — not rely on default Class vs instance locks. Fix: `private static final Object SHARED_LOCK` used by both methods.

---

keyPoints: Two threads can enter instance sync and static sync at same time
